facts.fact: Revises F197: on the storm night Kiran went up the Saddle alone with four loads of salt for the Dev people, lost the line within the hour and turned back to the waystone. Dilan, who had followed his tracks, rope-bound them there (knots on each wrist, names spoken to the stones, destination the third bend) and led him down the winter line. The ice shelf above the third bend gave way and they slid onto the road ice below it. Dilan cut his own rope; Kiran lay on the road ice, off the closed pass, until dawn, with his ear frozen to the glaze.
Rohan sees Kiran's torn ear in the passage as Kiran is led past, his eyes lingering on the missing rim, then chooses not to ask. Meera watches the choice.
Meera learned Dilan's name, the hymn and the rope end from Rohan in the hut, in a telling after chapter 9.
